method: Read comparison/profile/catalog components, URL helpers, edition data, all seven authored relationship records, comparison tests, representative paired profiles and prior usability guidance.
Inspected production comparison metadata and authored comparison URLs.

Live IAB checks on isolated audit origin http://127.0.0.1:4331/ToolWiki/: catalog/profile return; catalog/comparison/profile return; direct comparison return as positive control; CodeQL/PVS-Studio cost presentation.
Ran node --test tests/comparison.test.mjs: 7/7 passed. Did not rerun the full build.

No product edits, analyzer installation/execution, benchmark, or external source research. Upstream product entitlements were not independently reverified; related findings concern placement of existing repository qualifications.

findings.title: Profile return clears the comparison shortlist
findings.reader_task: Read a shortlisted tool's notes and return without rebuilding the comparison selection
reproduction: Open /ToolWiki/?language=Python&compare=tools%2Fruff%2Ctools%2Fmypy. The catalog shows Ruff and mypy checked and two selected.
Open Read notes on Ruff. The profile URL contains only catalog=language%3DPython.
Use Return to filtered results. URL is /ToolWiki/?language=Python; both checkboxes are unchecked and the selection tray is absent.
Reselect Ruff and mypy and open comparison, then follow its Ruff table header to the profile and use the same return link. The same selection loss occurs.
Positive control: direct comparison Return to filtered results retains compare=tools%2Fruff%2Ctools%2Fmypy and both boxes remain checked.
findings.evidence: Catalog profile links and comparison profile links pass sanitized filters but omit the selected IDs. ArticleContent deliberately calls catalogHref(base, [], context). This is separate from the Static/Dynamic category loss because it occurs on the All/Python catalog.
findings.impact: Readers lose a transient shortlist while using the explicit navigation provided for reviewing candidates. Browser Back can recover the earlier URL, so this is not permanent system-description data loss.
findings.recommendation: Carry the current normalized comparison IDs through profile navigation and use them in the profile's explicit catalog return. Preserve context when following related tool notes; a newly selected comparison must carry its current IDs. Coordinate the change with the category-context repair.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog -> profile -> explicit return preserves two or three selected IDs and filters.
Catalog -> comparison -> profile -> explicit return preserves the comparison's current IDs after additions/removals.
Direct comparison return continues to work.
Selections alone, without other filters, have a usable return path.
Unknown/duplicate IDs are normalized against catalog IDs and capped at three; old profile URLs without selection data remain valid.
Do not introduce arbitrary destination URLs or nested redirect context.
findings.compatibility: Additive allowlisted URL state; no saved-system format or local-storage requirement.
findings.prior_audit_status: New selection-loss evidence. Prior usability work promised and tested filter continuity; README explicitly promises selection persistence through filters/category links, not every profile visit. The observation is reported as workflow loss, not a fabricated broken documentation guarantee.

findings.title: Existing comparison links lack authored relationship guidance
findings.reader_task: Understand whether tools linked as a comparison are alternatives, complements, or different questions
evidence: The seven authored relationship records involve eleven distinct profiles. This is a scope count, not a target that every profile needs a pair.
Both mypy/Pyright and Trivy/OSV-Scanner have explicit comparison links in their profile bodies, but evaluating the current related-choice predicate for either pair returns no guidance.
The existing OSV profile explains that Trivy also has separate infrastructure-configuration workflows. The comparison's generic table cannot replace a short explanation of the decision.
Existing Ruff/mypy guidance correctly explains complementarity; no need to replace the current relationship mechanism.
findings.impact: Some deliberately linked comparisons stop at adjacent fields, while others explain why the pair is useful and how to choose. Readers must reconstruct the missing decision criteria.
findings.recommendation: Extend the existing toolChoices data for mypy/Pyright and Trivy/OSV-Scanner using checked, task-specific claims and links to maintained explanations. Distinguish shared jobs from complementary scopes; avoid rankings based on generic finding categories or raw issue counts.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the two existing comparison links renders a concise How these tools relate explanation.
Explain project/environment/configuration choices for the type checkers and input/scanner/interpretation boundaries for dependency scanners.
Use shared authored data for profile links and comparison guidance rather than copying a separate procedure.
Review primary sources before introducing new comparative capability claims; retain source/date scope.
dependencies: Primary-source confirmation for new comparative statements
findings.compatibility: Existing comparison URLs and IDs unchanged.
findings.prior_audit_status: Still-open extension of prior related-tool/companion-tool recommendations, not a regression.

findings.title: Cost qualifications are difficult to reach from the primary comparison row
findings.reader_task: Check whether a free option applies to a private or organization project
evidence: Live CodeQL/PVS comparison shows Free with limits, Paid in both primary Cost cells.
The details disclosure is closed by default. Existing costNote text and See edition details links are rendered only inside that disclosure.
Repository qualifications distinguish eligible public/personal use from private or organization use. This audit did not independently verify current upstream terms.
The visible Free with limits label is accurate and already warns of conditions; this is an access-to-context opportunity, not a false-free claim.
findings.impact: A decisive eligibility condition is placed under a section labeled technical details and sources instead of being directly reachable from the cost choice.
findings.recommendation: Make each primary Cost cell link to its profile's Cost and editions section, matching the catalog's pattern. Give restricted/free-with-limits entries a clear eligibility cue. Keep detailed notes available without copying every licensing paragraph into the primary table.
acceptance_criteria: Cost/eligibility details can be reached from the primary row without opening technical details.
CodeQL and PVS restricted-use caveats remain accurately scoped and accessible by keyboard.
Free, Free with limits, Paid and mixed values remain distinct; trials do not become free options.
Do not add unverified pricing or entitlement claims.
findings.compatibility: Rendering/navigation only; unchanged metadata and saved formats.
findings.prior_audit_status: New presentation opportunity; edition boundary protections remain correct.

findings.title: Comparison result summaries are uneven outside the four pilot profiles
findings.reader_task: Learn the output form and meaning before trying competing or complementary tools
findings.evidence: Live Ruff/mypy comparison shows a concrete diagnostics/rule/location description for Ruff but only Type errors for mypy. CodeQL/PVS shows concrete alerts/SARIF versus a list of finding categories. This matches decision.result falling back to findings. The richer format is optional and has four pilot entries, so the current fallback is not a schema violation.
findings.impact: The same row answers different questions across columns: output and interpretation for one tool, finding categories for another.
findings.recommendation: Deduplicate with newcomer N01 and reusable-content recommendations. Extend decision summaries in small, task-driven batches, keeping the editing guide's First try and execution-status requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Common comparison columns describe concrete output and its interpretation at comparable detail
Profile and comparison share one reviewed summary
No category list is presented as measured coverage
Illustrative and executed evidence remain separate
findings.compatibility: Use existing optional decision object; no schema migration.
findings.prior_audit_status: Continuation of the four-profile usability pilot.

corroborations.note: catalogParams excludes category; catalogHref root return causes category loss. No additional live category reproduction by this agent.
EditionComparison gates note and source under comparison.note; Polyspace has source but no note. General profile source remains.
Five promoted comparisons use hardcoded array positions. Keep explicit featured metadata recommendation with architecture finding.

positives: Separate tool records preserve free/paid capability boundaries instead of merging a product family into one filter result.
Comparison uses the same metadata as profiles and includes setup, environment, limits, detailed language scope, editions and sources.
Shared finding labels are explicitly said not to imply equal checks or coverage.
Ruff/mypy guidance clearly distinguishes complements; CodeQL/JBMC and RTAMT/PSY-TaLiRo distinguish different questions.
Unknown/duplicate tool IDs normalize safely; comparisons cap at three; bookmarked selections round-trip; direct comparison return keeps the current selection.
All seven existing comparison unit tests pass.
scope_limits: Live checks were desktop DOM/accessibility inspection, not mobile or keyboard-complete validation.
No human usability participants or analyzer performance/accuracy evaluation.
No changes to audit-origin system descriptions.
External current product capabilities and terms were not reverified by this lane.
Generic system-builder comparison context was considered but left to agents7/11; no unsupported finding that generic comparisons promise project-specific coverage.
Comparison getByLabel('Tool 1') automation lookup failed; the observed select ID worked. No product accessibility defect inferred from that automation mismatch.
